placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_wells, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by 3.0 m west of carpenter_south_water_store, which stands proud of the platted line and so cannot share a wall with the row. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

residents.research_note: THE OLDEST LIVING RESIDENT, AND THE ONE HOUSEHOLD IN THE PARCEL WHOSE ARRIVAL DATE THIS PROJECT HAD TO REFUSE TO GUESS - UNTIL A SENTENCE TURNED UP. Everything about Hubbard's later Chicago life was documented here and the date he first came was a fact everyone knew and nothing in data/sources/ stated, so it was carried as a conjecture citing nothing and left visibly empty rather than quietly filled: it was the case AGENTS.md rule 1 exists for. Hurlbut's American Fur Company chapter, read for T-0575 and cited by this record since T-0594, closes it - Montreal 13 May 1818, Mackinaw 4 July, Chicago the last day of October or the first of November - and the asymmetry that was worth leaving visible is now a smaller and more interesting one. The sentence is the COMPILER'S, not the man's: it stands outside the quotation marks in which Hubbard speaks four lines later, so a date this project had no source for at all now has a source of 1881 at rung 4, and the record says both things on its face rather than letting the citation look like an attestation. WHAT T-0753 ADDED, AND THE ONE THING IT COULD NOT. The same sentence carries more than the date T-0594 spent, and the rest of it is now on the card: `origin` reads "Windsor, Vermont, by way of Montreal" rather than the "Montreal" a careless reading of the field would have written, and the person carries a `birth_year` of 1802 with the birthplace in its note, both at the inferred grade the rung-4 layer supports and both corroborated by the man's own Calumet Club register entry of 1879. THE PARENTS WERE THE PART THAT DID NOT FIT, AND T-0849 RULED WHERE THEY GO. Hurlbut names Elizur and Abigail (Sage) Hubbard, and this dataset held no structure for them: the only relationship structure it has is the household-level `kin[]` block ratified on 2026-09-05, whose rows are reciprocal between two households IN THIS DATASET, and Hubbard's parents were living in Montreal, were never in this scene, and have no household here. T-0849 set out two readings - leave parentage outside the town as evidence, or invent an external kin row with `household` null - and on 2026-09-10 chose the first, on the ground that both rules `kin[]` enforces are rules about the FAR END. The inverse must be legal; the mirror row must exist. A row with no far end is not a weaker kin row, it is one with the entire checked part removed, and a graded name with nothing checking it is a note. The second reading would also have made every genealogical name in the corpus eligible for a residents layer that reconstructs a town on one day. SO THEY ARE A NOTE, AND THEY ARE ON THE CARD: the `origin` note above names them at inferred, under this record's own Hurlbut citation, which is the idiom the `birth_year` note uses for the birthplace and hh_harmon_elijah_d and hh_porter_jeremiah use for theirs. docs/PROVENANCE.md carries the rule for the next fact that has no field, and tools/validate.py now refuses a null-household kin row in the ruling's own words rather than reporting a household that failed to resolve - a message that would send a later run off to mint a Montreal household, which is the wrong answer twice over. The evidence is unmoved, in bk_afc_004's `entities`.

Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 7 times, as “PRUYNE P”, “PRUYNE PETER”, 1833-10-24 to 1836-06-24: 2 federal land entries — E2SW sec 30 T39N R13E; W2NW sec 30 T39N R13E and 2 lots in the platted town — lot 2 of block 58 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L2BL58CHIOT, as printed); lot 3 of block 17 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L3B17CHIOT, as printed) and 3 parcels of the school section — lot 1 of block 23 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 3 of block 119 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 8 of block 23 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 167.83 acres stated in all, for $17153.79 (ls0321, ls0323, ls0324, ls0858, ls0859, ls1436, ls1437). THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Woodworth, W.” (tax_1833_111, line 163). frontage.why: T-0078, and the owner's standing ruling of 2026-08-18 with it: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." The reference he supplied for this reach — "South Water Street in 1834", the south bank of the Main Branch — shows a CONTINUOUS WORKING ROW: one-storey log and frame buildings shoulder to shoulder facing the river, the street between them and the grassy bank, two-storey frame stores anchoring its east end. This block's anonymous roofs stood seven metres back from that frontage, a full lot apart, each nudged off the line by its own lateral offset and — because the placement rule takes its bearing from the way into the lot — facing the block's interior rather than the river. That is the shape of a distribution across a block, not of a street. They now stand ON the frontage: the line, its bearing and the end they pack back from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this recipe authors no coordinate for any of them. The 1.5 m setback is not a measurement of this frontage — it is the closest line the plat module's own lot margin allows, adopted so the street wall is one wall. NO ROOF IS ADDED: the run carries exactly the roofs the schedule dealt this block's frontage lots, with every id, family and dimension the one it already had. What the view drives is the treatment — a row on its line, facing the water — never a coordinate, and the side lot lines the row crosses between its own units were conjectural in every record this generator has ever written.
